title: observability: propagate request_id & trace for streaming, function-calls, structured-output, openai-compat
author: Miguel Ortega
description:
Motivation: Observability gaps were causing difficulty correlating streaming requests and function/tool invocations with traces and logs across the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR standardizes request_id propagation, W3C traceparent propagation, enriches structured logs with request/route metadata, and tags per-endpoint metrics so observability tools can reliably correlate user requests across layers (API gateway, compat adapter, runtime, tool invocations).

Summary of changes: unify request_id header handling (accept x-request-id, x-redwood-request-id, fallback generated UUID), propagate request_id into all streaming frames (SSE/WebSocket/HTTP chunked), attach request_id and trace_id to structured logs and metric labels, add span instrumentation around function/tool calls and include tool.name and call_id in spans, propagate W3C traceparent through the OpenAI compatibility adapter and inject when missing, surface per-route metric tags (route, method, compat_mode) for all API-level metrics.

Compatibility: OpenAI-compat layer maps incoming OpenAI-style headers ("OpenAI-Client-Request-Id") and standard headers to internal request_id. Consumers that rely on existing header names should continue working; we add new canonical header names (X-Redwood-Request-Id, traceparent) but respect existing headers if present. Streaming clients will see an additional top-level JSON field in structured stream events: "request_id" (backwards compatible for OpenAI-compat because the field is non-required and SDKs ignore unknown fields).

Testing: unit tests for header parsing/priority, end-to-end integration test for streaming with request_id propagation across gateway -> compat -> runtime -> tool. Added deterministic tracing test fixtures and a smoke canary that runs against dedicated in CI. Also added load test to ensure minimal latency overhead.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged; enable in staging, run canary on Dedicated (10% traffic) for 48h monitoring request/trace correlations, error rates, and metric cardinality. If stable, promote to 100% in 48h.

Related work: ENG-2401 (streaming stability & observability), ENG-2402 (function-calls tracing).

release_notes:
- Add canonical request_id propagation and support for OpenAI-style request ids
- Propagate W3C traceparent across the OpenAI compat adapter
- Structured logs now include request_id and trace_id for API surface
- Per-endpoint metric tags added to API metrics
- Instrumented function/tool calls with spans and call-level attributes
notes_for_operators: Feature is behind feature flag feature.observability.request_trace. When enabled, watch for increase in metric series and check 'api.request.trace_correlations' dashboard. Canary should be run at low traffic times if possible. If high-cardinality appears, disable feature and contact observability team.
changelog_entry: Observability: Request ID & trace propagation for API streaming and OpenAI-compat - adds structured log fields and per-route metric tags
migration_instructions: No mandatory migration. Clients that relied on custom header names can continue; recommended to read X-Redwood-Request-Id for canonical request id. To opt-in to richer observability, enable feature.observability.request_trace and run canary as described in PR description.
